title: The Employee That Worked on the Longest Task
statement:
A team has `n` employees with ids `0` to `n - 1`. They complete a sequence of tasks one after another, described by `logs`, where `logs[i] = [id, leaveTime]` says employee `id` handled task `i` and finished it at time `leaveTime`. Task `0` begins at time `0`, and every later task begins exactly when the previous one finishes, so task `i` lasts its finish time minus the previous task's finish time.

Return the id of the employee who handled the single longest task. When several tasks share the longest duration, return the smallest id among the employees who handled them.
constraints: The finish times logs[i][1] are strictly increasing
notes:
## Intuition

Each task's length depends only on its own finish time and the previous one, so a single walk through `logs` can measure every task while remembering when the last one ended. Along the way keep the best (longest) task found so far and who did it, settling ties in favour of the smaller id. A slower alternative records each employee's longest task and then scans all ids, but one pass already has all the information.

## Approach

1. Start with `longest = 0`, `start = 0` and `bestId = n`, an id larger than any real one.
2. For each `[id, leaveTime]`, the task's `duration` is `leaveTime - start`.
3. If `duration` beats `longest`, or equals it and `id` is smaller than `bestId`, record `duration` and `id`.
4. Set `start = leaveTime`, since the next task begins there.
5. Return `bestId`.

## Example 1, step by step

`logs = [[0,3],[2,5],[0,9],[1,15]]`. The durations are `3 - 0 = 3`, `5 - 3 = 2`, `9 - 5 = 4` and `15 - 9 = 6`. `bestId` becomes `0` (length 3), stays `0` after the length-2 task, stays `0` after the length-4 task (same employee, new `longest = 4`), and finally becomes `1` with length 6. The answer is `1`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(m), where m is `logs.length`: each task is measured once.
- Space: O(1).

## Pitfalls

- The first task starts at time `0`, so its length is its finish time, not zero.
- A task's length is the gap since the previous finish, not `leaveTime` itself.
- On a tie the smaller id wins even if its task came later; comparing with `>` alone keeps the earlier id instead.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `bestId` | id of the employee with the best task so far |
| `longest` | length of the longest task so far |
| `start` | time the current task began (the previous finish time) |
| `id`, `leaveTime` | the current log entry |
| `duration` | length of the current task |

narration.2: Start with an id larger than any real one so the first task always wins a tie check.
narration.3: No task has been measured yet, so the longest length is 0.
narration.4: The first task begins at time 0.
narration.6: Walk through the tasks in the order they were done.
narration.7: A task lasts from the previous finish time to its own finish time.
narration.8: Is this task longer, or equally long but done by a smaller id?
narration.12: The next task begins when this one ends.
narration.14: After every task, bestId holds the answer.
